hints.title: Information Theoretic Testing States
hints.text: Each testing interval provides states corresponding to the round in which a test subject expires or survives.

hints.title: Rounds Plus One Dimensionality
hints.text: If minutesToTest divided by minutesToDie equals T rounds, each pig can represent T plus 1 distinct states.

hints.title: Dimensional Base Encoding
hints.text: With p pigs and base b = T + 1, you can identify up to b raised to the power p buckets. Find the smallest integer p such that (minutesToTest // minutesToDie + 1) ** p >= buckets.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def poorPigs(self, buckets: int, minutesToDie: int, minutesToTest: int) -> int:
        rounds = minutesToTest // minutesToDie
        base = rounds + 1
        pigs = 0
        curr = 1
        while curr < buckets:
            curr *= base
            pigs += 1
        return pigs
```

variables: BUCKETS: number of liquid buckets to test
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating pig assignments directly explores combinatorially explosive decision trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Base-(rounds + 1) logarithmic scaling computes minimal pigs in O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Derive the (rounds + 1) state model using information theory.
